title: Inventory handoffs, TODOs, and cluster-compute work
description:
## Objective
Inspect the repository handoff documents and all project-level TODO/backlog sources, then report what remains to finish the Lewontin-paradox project now that heavyweight cluster computation is available. This is read-only research: do not modify project files.

## Scope
- Locate and read handoff/status/roadmap/TODO documents and relevant README or workflow notes.
- Reconcile their recommendations with the current repository state enough to flag stale, completed, duplicated, or contradictory items.
- Identify computation-heavy analyses that were previously blocked by local resources.
- For each remaining item, state inputs, code/workflow involved, expected outputs, dependencies, approximate resource shape (CPU/GPU, RAM, storage, walltime, array/parallel suitability), and a concrete validation/success criterion.
- Identify missing prerequisites such as datasets, software environments, credentials, scheduler details, or scientific decisions.
- Rank the work into: immediate cluster runs, preparatory engineering/data work, and later synthesis/writing.
- Recommend a dependency-ordered WG task graph, keeping tasks independently executable where possible.

## Validation
- [ ] All discoverable handoff and TODO documents are named and summarized.
- [ ] Claims are cross-checked against current repository state and clearly labeled as confirmed vs inferred.
- [ ] Every proposed cluster run has inputs, outputs, resource estimate, dependencies, and success criteria.
- [ ] The final task log contains a concise prioritized report and a proposed WG task graph.
- [ ] No repository files are modified.

DEFERRED COMPUTE + SYNTHESIS: Optional polarized SFS-B requires larger population samples, focal/outgroup FASTA, ancestral-state QC and frozen model; array by species/chromosome, ~4–8 CPU/32–64 GB/4–24 h, 0.1–1 TB; success on simulated truth plus stable B under polarization filters. title: Assess WFMASH SWEPGA and VCF-first Tier 3 design
description:
## Objective
Inspect locally available WFMASH and SWEPGA tooling, including repositories in the parent directory, and recommend the simplest scientifically defensible Tier 3 implementation strategy. This is read-only research; do not modify either repository.

## User direction
- Prefer annotation intersection with VCFs as the primary simple path. Treat the spoken term UCFs as likely VCFs, but flag evidence of any distinct intended format.
- WFMASH is available for pairwise alignment and should be considered for haplotype/assembly comparisons, fallbacks, or validation.
- SWEPGA is believed to have a repository in the parent directory and may provide reusable workflow components.
- The analyses are intentionally running on this cluster because laptop-scale execution is inadequate.

## Scope
- Locate the relevant parent-directory repositories/binaries and identify their actual command surfaces, inputs, outputs, dependencies, tests, and maturity.
- Determine exactly where WFMASH and SWEPGA fit the current tier3-implement-vgp, tier3-implement-popvcf, integration, and run tasks.
- Compare a VCF+GFF annotation-intersection primary workflow with pairwise H1/H2 assembly alignment, including callable denominators, phasing, reference bias, contig/annotation liftover, 4D W/S classification, compute cost, and validation.
- Recommend a primary path, fallback path, and one orthogonal concordance check, minimizing new code and operational complexity.
- State which existing paused WG task descriptions should change and provide exact proposed wording/acceptance-criterion changes.
- Assess whether the proposed data and methods can yield solid numbers for the study, separating strongly identifiable quantities from fragile or underpowered ones.

## Validation
- [ ] Local tooling claims cite confirmed repository paths and inspected entry points/tests.
- [ ] The VCF-first and alignment paths are compared on scientific validity and cluster cost.
- [ ] Reuse opportunities and integration risks for both tools are explicit.
- [ ] Recommendations include primary/fallback/QC paths and concrete edits to the paused WG tasks.
- [ ] Confidence is stated separately for pi, pi_W/pi_S, GC3/GC, SFS-B, and causal interpretation.
- [ ] No files are modified.

Starting local-tool and Tier 3 workflow assessment; will inspect repositories, paused task descriptions, command surfaces, tests, and scientific trade-offs.

Located and inspected WFMASH at /moosefs/erikg/wfmash and SweepGA at /moosefs/erikg/sweepga. No scientific UCF token or .ucf format occurs in the study or either tool repository; UCF is therefore almost certainly a transcription of VCF. Repository worktrees remain unmodified by this assessment; pre-existing uncommitted SweepGA documentation/install changes are untouched.

TOOLING AUDIT — WFMASH. Confirmed source repository /moosefs/erikg/wfmash at f22d4a566579534c50274e350958ed2d5d9b0a87 on erikg/guix-build-env, clean. Entry point is src/interface/main.cpp with flags defined in src/interface/parse_args.hpp:78-138 and executable declared in CMakeLists.txt:294-305. README.md:9-36 describes MashMap/minmer mapping followed by base-level WFA; README.md:38-64 gives target/query FASTA to PAF; README.md:112-120 gives PAF or SAM, optional MD, threads and indexes; README.md:123-125 requires a target .fai. Base-level PAF carries cg:Z CIGAR in src/common/wflign/src/wflign_patch.cpp:2240-2252 and optional MD around 2405. It is an aligner, not a variant caller. The bundled scripts/fasta+paf2vcf.sh:17-29 obtains VCF only by adding seqwish and vg deconstruct, an unnecessarily heavy graph path for Tier 3. Source builds exist at build/bin/wfmash and build-static/bin/wfmash; both report v0.24.2-12-ge040aa10. By contrast /home/erikg/.guix-profile/bin/wfmash resolves to Guix wfmash-0.12.5-1+0222f7c and its version flag prints only a newline, so the profile binary must not be silently used. Build requirements are C++17 plus CMake, zlib, GSL, HTSlib, lzma, bzip2, threads and OpenMP at CMakeLists.txt:16-39 and README.md:229-250. Six CTest cases are declared at CMakeLists.txt:445-472 for timing, SAM, mapping coverage, PAF validity, MAF and index reuse; both existing builds enumerate all six. CI builds and runs CTest on Linux and macOS at .github/workflows/test_on_push.yml:13-78. Full tests were intentionally not executed because their declared working directory writes products into the tool repository.

TOOLING AUDIT — SWEEPGA. The actual spelling is SweepGA, repository /moosefs/erikg/sweepga at 018e4ce49d2c125820e0ac50dc5feaa02d423683, package/binary version 0.1.1. Current source has pre-existing local changes in README.md, docs/BUILD-NOTES.md, install.sh and scripts/build-clean.sh; none were touched. Cargo.toml:1-10 identifies the package, Cargo.toml:25-45 pins Rust dependencies including git revisions of fastga-rs and wfmash-rs, and Cargo.toml:47-53 declares sweepga plus alnstats. README.md:3-22 and 43-66 describe FASTA or PAF/1aln input, FastGA default or WFMASH backend, and PAF/1aln output. src/main.rs:104-169 implements content detection; src/wfmash_integration.rs:28-109 configures the wfmash-rs backend and lines 113-151 index FASTA and emit temporary/direct PAF. Current binary help additionally confirms batching, max-disk, temp-dir, PAF filtering, AGC, pair lists, resume ledgers and joblist output. Joblist is implemented at src/joblist.rs:1-74, but lines 35-39 warn stem collisions and its emitted shell is not quoted. Pair/resume flags are at src/cli.rs:316-399. PAF filtering preserves original cg, MD and other tags by selecting and rewriting original lines at src/paf_filter.rs:1688-1725; a /tmp smoke retained NM, cg and MD exactly and exited 0. alnstats accepts one/two PAF or 1aln inputs and optional per-pair detail but has no version flag. Cargo test surface is substantial: 33 integration files, 250 test annotations and 13 ignored annotations; tests/README.md:5-59 distinguishes CI library tests from slower/manual binary tests, tests/test_determinism.rs:1-15 documents a slow ignored full-pipeline check, and tests/test_end_to_end.rs:131-208 documents yeast coverage tests skipped in CI due FastGA races. CI builds release and runs library plus a targeted WFMASH/FastGA integration test on Linux/macOS at .github/workflows/ci.yml:13-57. This is promising but young workflow code, not a diversity estimator or variant caller.

MATURITY AND REUSE JUDGMENT. WFMASH has the narrower, mature command surface needed for one H1/H2 pair and already emits base-level PAF CIGAR; pin the repository build revision and command line. SweepGA adds useful PAF tag-preserving filters, disk telemetry, batching, pair ledgers, joblist and alnstats, but its default is FastGA, default scaffolding is enabled, its WFMASH backend is a separately pinned wfmash-rs revision rather than the inspected local WFMASH binary, and some slow binary tests are excluded from ordinary CI. For one diploid pair per Slurm array element, those layers add version and filtering semantics without reducing Tier 3 code. Do not make SweepGA a required dependency. Permit alnstats or a precisely pinned SweepGA PAF-filter command as optional alignment QC only after a pilot proves unchanged SNP counts and callable coverage. No UCF token or .ucf format occurs in the study, WFMASH or SweepGA source; UCF is treated as a spoken transcription of VCF.
Requirement update accepted: all Tier 3 environment/install management will use GNU Guix; micromamba/conda paths will be removed from proposed task wording.

GUIX AUDIT. Cluster command /home/erikg/.guix-profile/bin/guix is GNU Guix 1.4.0-7.44bbfc2. guix describe resolves current channel commit 44bbfc24e4bcc48d0e3343cd3d83452721af8c36. /var/guix/daemon-socket/socket exists and guix-daemon is live with max-jobs=6 and substitutes from cuirass.genenetwork.org, ci.guix.gnu.org and bordeaux.guix.gnu.org. The user channel file adds rustup without a commit, so it must not be inherited for Tier 3. The locally demonstrated pinning convention is /moosefs/erikg/likegt/.guix/channels.scm:9-19, which pins Guix 44bbfc24 and guix-bioinformatics 48af9393; Tier 3 only needs the pinned Guix channel unless a package uniquely requires guix-bioinformatics. The current Guix package universe provides bash 5.1.16, Python and python-pysam 0.20.0, pyfaidx 0.7.2.1, Biopython 1.80, numpy 1.23.2, pandas 1.4.4, scipy 1.10.1, scikit-allel 1.3.5, bcftools 1.14, samtools 1.14, htslib 1.16, bedtools 2.30.0, vcftools 0.1.16, curl, wget, parallel and pigz. A dry-run of this base Tier 3 package set succeeded. cyvcf2, malariagen-data, SweepGA, Apptainer and Nextflow are absent; avoid them in the primary design. Python Zarr exists but drags a much larger closure and is unnecessary if Ag1000G is staged as VCF.

GUIX TOOL PACKAGING RISKS. /moosefs/erikg/wfmash/manifest.scm:1-23 is a valid Guix shell manifest and dry-runs successfully, but it contains build tools rather than an immutable WFMASH package. /moosefs/erikg/wfmash/guix.scm:164-188 packages the entire current checkout with local-file and derives its version from live git state, so it is not portable provenance. Worse, both advertised dry-runs, guix build -f guix.scm and guix build -L . wfmash-gcc-git, fail on this cluster pin because gnu packages crates-check is unavailable; the latter also exposes a module-name collision. The upstream pinned Guix channel only offers old WFMASH 0.8.1, while the user profile contains 0.12.5 and the inspected repository build is v0.24.2 lineage. Foundations therefore needs a small local package definition using git-fetch at f22d4a566579534c50274e350958ed2d5d9b0a87, recursive submodule WFA2-lib 49c255df126ee536fe92caff7a9f7c183ec3ff29, fixed content hash, cmake-build-system and the known C++ dependencies; it must not import the current checkout-based guix.scm. SweepGA has no Guix definition. Its Cargo.lock contains four pinned git dependency families, and build.rs:1-70 writes helper binaries into the user cache while lines 190-209 delete old cache directories, which conflicts with a pure Guix build. Packaging it would require vendored Cargo sources plus patching cache/output behavior. Since SweepGA is optional QC only, the simplest defensible choice is not to package or invoke it in Tier 3.

GUIX REPRODUCIBILITY RECOMMENDATION. Replace analysis/envs/tier3.yaml with analysis/guix/channels.scm, analysis/guix/manifest.scm and analysis/guix/packages/wfmash.scm. Pin the Guix channel commit and every custom source commit/hash. Keep the manifest minimal: shell/core utilities, nss-certs, Python, pytest, pysam, pyfaidx, Biopython, numpy, pandas, scipy, bcftools, samtools, htslib, bedtools, vcftools, curl, wget, parallel, pigz and wfmash-tier3; do not include micromamba, conda, cyvcf2, malariagen-data or SweepGA. Reproducible form: $HOME/.guix-profile/bin/guix time-machine -C analysis/guix/channels.scm -- shell -m analysis/guix/manifest.scm --pure --preserve=SLURM_.* --preserve=TIER3_.* --preserve=TMPDIR -- COMMAND. Before arrays, realize a shared GC root with the same time-machine and guix shell --root, record resolved guix describe, derivation/store paths and tool versions, and run a compute-node sbatch smoke that imports Python modules, indexes tiny FASTA/VCF fixtures and executes WFMASH. Direct Guix shell is primary. Only if compute nodes cannot access the shared daemon/store may integration build a checksum-recorded guix pack squashfs from the same manifest and use a Guix-declared Singularity compatibility runtime; no hand-built or Conda container.

SCIENTIFIC COMPARISON — VCF+GFF PRIMARY. Require an exact, checksum-locked reference tuple: FASTA, GFF/GTF, VCF/BCF and cohort callable/accessibility mask from the same assembly accession. Generate the full set of eligible 4D third-position coordinates from FASTA+GFF after frozen transcript, CDS phase, strand and genetic-code rules, then intersect the full callable set, not only variant rows. For each callable site compute unbiased pairwise diversity from called allele counts and include accessible invariant sites as zero; missing genotypes affect the per-site chromosome count. A variant-only VCF without an all-sites/gVCF or explicit cohort mask cannot identify the denominator and must be rejected for pi, not treated as callable reference sequence. Population pi does not require phased genotypes. This path avoids assembly contig pairing and liftover entirely when accessions match, minimizes reference-coordinate code, and costs roughly 2-8 CPU, 16-64 GB and 1-12 hours/species depending on VCF size, with tens to low hundreds of GB total scratch for pre-called data. Risks are reference mapping/variant-call bias, resource-specific filters, inbred/haploid/diploid semantics and heterogeneous masks; control them through exact manifests, population-specific filters, fixed sample policy, repeat/mappability masks, missingness/QC and an independent allele-count check.

SCIENTIFIC COMPARISON — H1/H2 ALIGNMENT FALLBACK. Direct pinned WFMASH aligns H2 to annotated H1 and emits base-level PAF cg CIGAR. A fallback estimator must traverse CIGAR plus both FASTAs, count SNV mismatches only at uniquely mapped one-to-one syntenic positions, and define the denominator as alignable A/C/G/T positions after removing gaps, overlaps, ambiguous mappings, repeats, contig ends and declared structural-variant neighborhoods. That is an alignable denominator, not sequencing callability, so it preferentially drops divergent/rearranged sequence and can bias heterozygosity downward. H1 annotation supplies 4D sites; H2 coordinates are projected through CIGAR. A mismatched GFF requires explicit validated liftover and should normally be rejected. Assembly phasing is essential and must be screened for haplotype collapse, switches, duplicated haplotigs, contamination, primary/alternate imbalance and contig pairing; deposited variants do not need haplotype phase for per-site diversity. Reference-conditioned W/S classes also require a reference-swap sensitivity because H1 versus H2 is arbitrary. Conservative cluster shape remains 4-8 CPU, 32-64 GB, 8-24 hours/species and roughly 200-500 GB for 40-60 diploid assemblies, versus the much cheaper deposited-VCF path. WFMASH cluster chunking exists at README.md:481-525, but one pair/species Slurm arrays should pilot before adding mapping-chunk fanout.

4D W/S INTERPRETATION. Freeze one statistic name and direction, preferably pi_S_over_pi_W, because current task text alternates pi_W/pi_S and pi_S/pi_W. Grouping sites by the current reference base W=A/T or S=G/C yields reference-conditioned 4D diversity, not mutation-direction counts and not an estimate of B. It is descriptive and can be computed without an outgroup, but reference composition, mutation bias, codon usage and ascertainment can affect it. Report numerator, denominator, callable site count and bootstrap interval for each class, plus reciprocal only for presentation. Directional W-to-S versus S-to-W SFS and B require ancestral polarization, an outgroup, polarization-error filters, sufficiently large samples and a demographic model; phasing is still unnecessary for the folded per-site pi. This should remain optional/deferred rather than being inferred from reference-conditioned classes.

RECOMMENDED THREE-PATH DESIGN. PRIMARY: exact-reference deposited population or diploid VCF/BCF plus FASTA, GFF and explicit cohort/diploid callable mask; use shared Python/pysam 4D and allele-count code, with bcftools/bedtools only for normalization and interval cross-checks. FALLBACK: for eligible phased VGP H1/H2 assemblies lacking a defensible deposited VCF+mask, direct pinned WFMASH to raw base-level PAF followed by a small Tier 3 CIGAR/mask parser; label the result individual SNV heterozygosity per alignable base, never population pi. ORTHOGONAL CONCORDANCE: choose at least one exact VGP individual with both deposited heterozygous calls/callability and H1/H2 assemblies, compute total and 4D W/S estimates by both paths blind to each other, and require predeclared agreement on their common callable intersection with discordance stratified by repeats, gaps and contigs. This validates both the VCF annotation intersection and alignment fallback. SweepGA is not part of any primary estimator; optional tag-preserving filtering may be explored only if the raw and retained PAFs, counts and denominators are all preserved.

EXACT TASK EDIT — tier3-freeze-decisions. Replace Description with: "Freeze every Tier 3 scientific, access and execution policy before implementation. For each diversity dataset require an exact assembly-accession tuple for FASTA, annotation, VCF/BCF and callable/accessibility source; define whether the source is all-sites, gVCF or a cohort mask, and reject variant-only data without a defensible invariant denominator. Freeze sample/population/ploidy/downsampling rules, canonical-transcript/CDS-phase/genetic-code rules, the precise reference-conditioned 4D statistic name and direction, eligibility for deposited-VCF primary versus WFMASH H1/H2 fallback, common-callable concordance tolerances, and whether polarized SFS-B is deferred. Freeze GNU Guix as the sole environment manager, the channel commits, custom WFMASH commit, compute-node daemon/store access, scratch and data access. Containers are allowed only as a Guix-built compatibility fallback. Record decisions and a machine-readable schema." Add Validation: "Every diversity row declares same-reference FASTA/GFF/VCF/mask provenance or is ineligible for pi"; "No variant-only VCF is assigned an invariant denominator by assumption"; "pi_S_over_pi_W versus any reciprocal and reference-conditioned versus polarized quantities are unambiguous"; "Guix channel commits, WFMASH source commit and numeric concordance tolerances are frozen"; "A compute-node job confirms Guix daemon/store, data egress or prestaging, and scratch"; "No Conda, micromamba or hand-built container is approved."

EXACT TASK EDIT — tier3-foundations-manifest. Replace analysis/envs/tier3.yaml in File scope with analysis/guix/channels.scm, analysis/guix/manifest.scm, analysis/guix/packages/wfmash.scm and analysis/validate_tier3_guix.sh. title: Validate IMPG BCF generation from haplotype alignments
description:
## Objective
Identify and validate the locally installed IMPG tooling for generating region-queryable BCF/VCF from a WFMASH alignment of haplotype A to haplotype B. Establish whether this is the simplest assembly-derived variant path for Tier 3a. Do not modify project or tooling repositories; any generated test data must stay in temporary scratch.

## User direction
- For a single haplotype A/B genome pair, WFMASH alignment is expected to be stable.
- The alignment defines or feeds an implicit graph; IMPG is expected to query regions and emit BCF/VCF.
- The resulting normalized variant representation should feed the same GFF/callable-site annotation intersection used for pre-called VCFs.

## Scope
- Resolve the exact tool spelling, installed binary/repository/version, documentation, command surface, input alignment requirements, implicit-graph/index representation, region-query behavior, and actual BCF/VCF output capability.
- Determine whether IMPG consumes WFMASH PAF directly and which tags/options (cg, cs, MD, primary alignments, filtering) are required.
- Using existing small fixtures or a synthetic two-haplotype example in temporary scratch, run the smallest end-to-end path: FASTA A+B -> WFMASH alignment -> IMPG graph/index/query -> BCF/VCF.
- Validate the output with bcftools or an equivalent independent parser: header/contigs, coordinates, REF/ALT orientation, SNP/indel normalization, genotype/ploidy/phasing, region boundaries, duplicate/overlap handling, and round-trip agreement with known truth.
- Explain callable-denominator construction and how GFF/4D W/S annotations in the reference coordinate system should intersect the emitted variants.
- Compare this path with WFMASH -> seqwish -> vg deconstruct and direct PAF parsing on complexity, correctness, storage, and cluster cost.
- Provide exact recommended edits to the paused tier3-implement-vgp, tier3-foundations-manifest, tier3-integrate-cluster, and tier3-run-vgp task descriptions.
- All environment and dependency management must use pinned GNU Guix manifests/channels; do not introduce conda/micromamba.

## Validation
- [ ] Exact IMPG identity/version/path and BCF/VCF capability are confirmed from local code/help/docs.
- [ ] A scratch-only end-to-end example produces standards-valid BCF/VCF or records a concrete, reproducible blocker.
- [ ] Independent validation demonstrates coordinate, allele, genotype, normalization, and region-query semantics.
- [ ] Required WFMASH output tags/filtering and callable-denominator rules are explicit.
- [ ] The recommended primary/fallback path and exact paused-task edits are recorded in the final task log.
- [ ] Guix packaging requirements and version pins are specified.
- [ ] No repository files are modified.

title: Verify exact SweepGA to IMPG handoff
description:
Establish and demonstrate the exact SweepGA-to-IMPG handoff before Tier 3A acquisition or production analysis resumes. Inspect the parent SweepGA repository and installed/local IMPG source, help, and examples. The conceptual division is fixed: SweepGA performs whole-haplotype H1-versus-H2 mapping and -n 1:1 constrains query:target mapping multiplicity; IMPG consumes that mapping, performs native implicit-graph partitioning, focuses queries on regions, and emits VCF/BCF. Do not move graph partitioning into SweepGA or a preprocessing window scheme.

Use the exact H1-native genome annotation to define biologically interpretable IMPG query targets, prioritizing coding genes/CDS with valid contig and phase provenance. Query annotation-derived regions through IMPG after graph partitioning. Merge overlapping target intervals for efficient querying where appropriate, use only context/padding justified by IMPG behavior, and deterministically trim/deduplicate results back to annotation targets. Preserve feature identities and track excluded or unqueryable genes. Coding/CDS estimates must not be labeled genome-wide.

Determine the exact meaning of SweepGA -n 1:1 from authoritative source/help, including query/target hit semantics, ties/repeats, and output format. Determine exact IMPG commands and accepted mapping format for graph ingestion, native partitioning, regional queries, and VCF/BCF extraction. Verify whether alternative caps use forms such as -n 5:5 and -n 10:10 rather than assuming. Use GNU Guix and record channel commit, manifest, builds, versions, and commands.

Run the end-to-end proof on representative natively annotated coding regions from at least one staged biological H1/H2 pair. Start at sweepga -n 1:1 and end at normalized, indexed VCF/BCF from IMPG partition/query. Validate selected SNPs/indels directly against H1 and H2 sequence and compute a nonzero callable denominator. Synthetic truth is not required and is not a completion gate. Preserve downloaded biological FASTAs and do not endorse the prior WFMASH-first extraction design.

title: Plan vertebrate effective-population-size strategy
description:
Develop a rigorous, execution-ready strategy for adding effective-population-size information to the vertebrate scale-out, using analysis/vertebrate_scaleout_origin_inventory.md and its identified synchronized guidance as controlling inputs. The goal is to support Lewontin-paradox analyses without circularly deriving an independent predictor from the same diversity outcome. This is planning only: do not launch large demographic inference jobs or bulk population-data downloads.

Compare viable methods against data actually available across vertebrates and keep their input and estimand contracts distinct:
- PSMC: one callable diploid genome from one biological individual, represented by diploid consensus/heterozygous sites plus a reference-matched callable mask; estimates a piecewise pairwise coalescent-rate/history for the two homologs, initially in coalescent/mutation-scaled units, with limited recent-time resolution.
- MSMC2 (distinguish it from legacy MSMC): multiple accurately phased haplotypes from one or more individuals plus per-haplotype/reference-matched masks; estimates within- and cross-coalescence-rate histories and related scaled summaries, with sample-count, phasing, switch-error, and recent/deep-time limitations stated.
- SMC++: multiple same-population diploid samples in reference-matched VCF/BCF or equivalent genotype input, masks, sample/population assignments, and any distinguished lineages required by the selected analysis; combines SFS/linkage information to estimate population-size histories or split models, with polarization/phasing requirements stated only where the chosen mode actually requires them.
- Other defensible methods, including LD-, temporal-, pedigree-, SFS-, or site-pattern-based approaches: document their distinct samples, inputs, estimands, time windows, identifiability, and assumptions rather than grouping them under generic Ne.

For every method specify biological sampling unit, minimum and preferred sample count, raw-read/genotype requirements, coverage, reference identity, phasing, callable masks, recombination/mutation assumptions, time resolution, primary estimand, computational/I/O/storage cost, software/Guix provenance, failure modes, and expected eligible species coverage. Determine what is and is not inferable from one phased H1/H2 assembly. Do not assume that two deposited assembly haplotypes constitute a callable diploid genotype: require evidence they are homologs from the same individual, exact-reference compatibility, retained heterozygosity, callable-site construction, and method-valid input generation; otherwise classify them as assembly/composition data only.

Enforce the circularity rule at data-model and analysis levels. PSMC/MSMC2/SMC++ and any estimator driven by the same heterozygosity, SFS, or pi observations are outcomes/derived genomic summaries, not independent predictors in a model whose response is that same pi. Explicitly prohibit estimating Ne as pi/(4*mu), or an equivalent transformation of the response, and then regressing pi on that Ne or interpreting it as independent support. Genomic histories may be used descriptively, for temporal-shape/clustering summaries, method validation, non-causal decomposition, or prespecified sensitivity analyses that acknowledge shared data; prevent leakage into the primary independent-covariate analysis.

Separate quantities retained in coalescent-scaled units, such as theta, lambda(t), tau, or Ne(t)*mu as appropriate to the method, from calendar time and absolute Ne. Every conversion to absolute Ne/time must state the exact convention and ploidy, mutation rate per generation, generation time, recombination assumptions if used, calibration source/population, taxonomic transfer rule, and uncertainty propagation. Report posterior/interval or scenario distributions instead of point estimates when mutation rate, generation time, or model calibration is uncertain; never hide borrowed-rate uncertainty.

Evaluate genuinely independent alternatives and covariates: temporal/LD/pedigree Ne where their data are independent of the response being modeled; direct mutation rates and generation times; census abundance, range size, density, body mass, fecundity, longevity, reproductive mode, dispersal, and other ecological/life-history predictors. For literature/ecological records capture original source/DOI/URL, quoted estimand definition, method, population and geography, sampling and measurement dates, units, interval/error, sample size, life stage/sex where relevant, extraction method, curator/retrieval date, taxon authority/identifier, synonym resolution, match distance, transfer rationale, and quality flag. Do not collapse contemporary, variance, inbreeding, linkage, long-term coalescent, and census quantities into a single Ne column.

Propose a tiered data model: primary covariates demonstrably independent of the analyzed pi observations; secondary literature/ecological Ne with provenance and uncertainty; coalescent-scaled genomic histories; derived absolute histories with mutation/generation-time scenarios; and excluded/circular or taxonomically ambiguous estimates. Recommend a practical vertebrate-wide primary strategy plus smaller, explicitly eligible high-quality subsets for absolute Ne and population demographic inference. Define population/species/reference/taxonomy joins, temporal alignment, missingness, exclusions, measurement-error models, phylogenetic handling, sensitivity analyses, and claims each tier can support.

Give a phased acquisition and inference proposal with pilot truth cases, per-method species counts/ranges, GNU Guix environments, CPU/memory/wall/scratch/persistent-storage/I/O estimates, validation thresholds, failure criteria, and go/no-go reviews. Use authoritative primary literature and official method/documentation sources with retrieval dates and citations.

## Validation
- Provide a method comparison matrix that separately covers PSMC, MSMC2, SMC++, and other viable methods: biological samples, exact input representation, masks/phasing/coverage, estimand, scaled versus absolute output, time window, compute/I/O/storage, assumptions, failure modes, and expected data availability.
- Audit available vertebrate data and state what is inferable from one phased diploid H1/H2 assembly, raw reads, one callable diploid genotype, multiple phased genomes, and multi-sample population VCFs; reject invalid assembly-to-demography shortcuts.
- State which Ne quantities/covariates are independent of the analyzed pi observations and which are circular, and enforce the prohibition on deriving Ne from the same pi then treating it as an independent predictor of pi.
- Recommend a primary phylogenetically aware analysis using independent ecological/life-history or independently measured demographic covariates, with prespecified, clearly non-independent sensitivity/descriptive uses of PSMC/MSMC2/SMC++.
- Keep coalescent-scaled quantities separate from absolute Ne/calendar time and define mutation-rate/generation-time sourcing, ploidy/convention checks, taxonomic transfer, and propagated uncertainty/scenario distributions.
- Define literature/ecological source provenance, estimand vocabulary, species/population/reference/taxonomy matching, measurement dates, uncertainty, missingness, quality flags, and exclusion policies.

title: Audit VGP demography inputs
description:

This task is metadata and literature/source audit only: download no bulk reads or VCFs, submit no compute, and run no PSMC, MSMC2, SMC++, or other demographic inference.

Classify eligibility separately and do not collapse the methods:
- PSMC: one demonstrably diploid callable genome/consensus retaining heterozygosity, a compatible mask, and sufficient individual/read/reference/coverage provenance.
- MSMC2: the required number of demonstrably accurate, mutually comparable phased haplotypes/genomes with masks and individual/population relationships.
- SMC++: a multi-sample population genotype/VCF dataset with sample identities, population definition, reference compatibility, masks, and required QC.
- Independent contemporary or literature Ne: LD, temporal, pedigree, variance, or inbreeding estimates with estimand, population, geography, time, uncertainty, and source provenance.
- Independent ecological/life-history covariates and census measures.

Same-individual/phasing evidence required for Tier3A diversity does not by itself establish PSMC, MSMC2, or SMC++ eligibility. Record method-specific missing requirements rather than promoting a generic demographic-ready flag.

For each selected species, search authoritative repositories and primary literature for raw-read availability, individual relationships, population genotypes, sample sizes, phasing, coverage, exact reference identity, callable masks, mutation rate, generation time, recombination information, existing Ne estimates, population/geography, uncertainty, and provenance. title: Design gene-conversion evidence program
description:
Design a separate evidence-tiered program for gene conversion and GC-biased gene conversion with four non-interchangeable branches. Direct evidence uses complete pedigrees, transmitted parental haplotypes, sperm, or gametes to estimate callable meiotic events, tract length, crossover association, and GC transmission distortion. Population evidence uses multi-individual, same-population genotypes to compare polarized or polarization-aware WS and SW allele-frequency spectra and estimate B while controlling mutation bias, demography, linkage, recombination, structure, and polarization error. Historical phylogenetic evidence uses orthologous neutral, fourfold, coding, and noncoding alignments from close clades and outgroups, including semi-complete genomes, to estimate branch-specific WS/SW substitution asymmetry and long-term gBGC-like bias. Non-allelic evidence tests conversion among paralogs or segmental duplications with copy-aware orthology/paralogy and GENECONV-like nulls; it is not meiotic allelic conversion.

State the identifiability boundary for every branch. H1/H2 pairs alone can describe heterozygous WS/SW states and candidate clusters, but without parent-of-origin, gamete transmission, population frequencies, or outgroup polarization they cannot establish conversion direction, event transmission, or GC-biased transmission. Historical substitution bias is not a count of direct events. Population B is model-dependent and not a direct tract rate. Paralog homogenization is not allelic gBGC. Direct human or single-species estimates may supply bounded sensitivity priors but must not be extrapolated across vertebrates as measured rates. Separate gBGC sensitivity from demographic interpretation because gBGC can mimic selection and distort site-frequency and substitution summaries.

Inventory public datasets and select one direct pilot, two VGP close-clade phylogenetic pilots plus alternates, at least one feasible population design plus alternate, and at least one feasible non-allelic design plus alternate. The present execution graph contains direct and phylogenetic pilot tasks only: population and non-allelic branches remain design-only unless separately authorized tasks are added. The synthesis must label them not measured rather than infer them from H1/H2.

title: Repair VGP pilot authorization
description:

Start and sustain the real official VGP Freeze 1 assembly mirror under /moosefs/erikg/vgp/freeze1 using the frozen remote inventory of 43,371 files and approximately 3.917 TB. Recheck actual filesystem free space and write permissions, then transfer with resumable official-source tooling, checksums, content-addressed reuse, partial staging, quarantine, and atomic promotion. Make verified files available incrementally.

The user explicitly authorized tens of TB. Remove the obsolete QUOTA_UNAVAILABLE and arbitrary total-byte caps as policy gates. Real ENOSPC, permission, network, or checksum failures remain operational errors. Use moderate concurrency and avoid metadata storms.

- Transfer and verify real payload bytes; zero-byte completion is forbidden.
- Report exact inventory, progress, throughput, retries, verified and quarantined bytes.

title: Build BGZF VGP assembly view
description:
Build a reusable BGZF-compressed and indexed view of every assembly FASTA in the completed VGP Freeze 1 mirror. Preserve the immutable byte-for-byte upstream mirror under /moosefs/erikg/vgp/freeze1. Write derived files only under /moosefs/erikg/vgp/derived/freeze1-bgzf while preserving source-relative accession paths.

Inventory every assembly FASTA from the terminal mirror manifest. Detect whether each source is uncompressed FASTA, ordinary gzip, or already valid BGZF. Reuse or hardlink an existing BGZF object only when format and content verification pass; otherwise stream-decompress and recompress with pinned htslib bgzip without materializing a full uncompressed assembly on shared storage. Generate valid .gzi and samtools .fai indexes. Annotations and other source files remain unchanged in this task.

Run through pinned GNU Guix and resumable Slurm arrays with input-size-based CPU, memory, scratch, and I/O limits. Use node-local scratch, atomic promotion, content-addressed reuse, moderate metadata concurrency, reason-coded retries, and no destructive modification of source objects. Record a stable configuration variable and manifest so future VGP scale-out jobs preferentially consume the BGZF view while existing pilot jobs continue on their immutable inputs.

## Validation
- Closed-world account for every mirrored assembly FASTA as reused, converted, failed, or explicitly excluded.
- For every promoted BGZF, verify the decompressed SHA-256, byte count, sequence count, contig names and lengths against the source stream.
- Verify BGZF structure, EOF marker, .gzi, .fai, samtools faidx random-access probes, and source-to-derived provenance.
- Report total source bytes, derived bytes, compression ratio, CPU-hours, peak memory, scratch, failures, and retries.
- Promote only complete triplets of BGZF, .gzi, and .fai atomically.
- Produce a machine-readable shared-resource manifest and handoff under the repository analysis tree; never place bulk data in git.
- Completion requires real derived BGZF payloads. Zero-output completion is forbidden.

Size memory, CPUs, scratch, and wall time per genome with substantial headroom. Do not reintroduce an arbitrary global cap. Retry resource failures with increased allocations. Allow independent pairs to continue when one fails.

title: Scale real VGP biological analyses
description:
After a real pilot GO or bounded CONDITIONAL_GO, run the validated core workflow across every eligible same-individual mutually comparable VGP H1/H2 pair in the frozen catalog. Process in resumable Slurm waves with per-genome resources derived from real pilot telemetry. Compute callable diversity and assembly-derived PSMC for all confidence tiers; add exact native annotation partitions where available.

Do not require annotations, external Ne, final QV, BUSCO, raw reads, repeat reports, or k-mer audits as universal core gates. Track them as confidence covariates. Hard failures remain exact provenance, integrity, alignment multiplicity, reconstruction, callability, or concrete execution errors.

## Validation
- Submit real biological jobs and account for every catalog pair.
- Produce verified per-pair estimates and scale-out telemetry.
- Zero-job completion is forbidden.
- Preserve same-pair pi and PSMC non-independence and all scenario uncertainty.

Canonical shared VGP root: /moosefs/erikg/vgp. The legacy project-specific root /moosefs/erikg/lewontin-paradox-data/vgp is migration input only: inventory and reuse any verified partial objects, then move or relink them without redownload. Do not create new canonical data under a Lewontin-paradox-named directory. Record the canonical root in every emitted manifest so other projects can link to it.

FastGA scratch-working-directory contract: every SweepGA or FastGA stage must create and validate a private working directory under node-local /scratch for the Slurm job, stage its FASTAs and indexes there, export TMPDIR, TMP, and TEMP to that directory, and cd into it before invoking the aligner. Live validation must prove /proc/cwd and every FastGA _tmp_, pair, index, and intermediate file resolve under /scratch. A submit-worktree, MooseFS, /tmp-rootfs, or input-directory FastGA temporary path is a hard infrastructure error requiring clean cancellation and retry, not a biological pair failure. Atomic promotion and guarded cleanup occur only after verified alignment success.

title: Run three-pair VGP reliability pilot
description:
Demonstrate pipeline reliability on three representative same-individual H1/H2 pairs: one previously successful exact-annotation pair, one prior FastGA execution failure, and one prior IMPG graph/FASTA identifier failure. Freeze the three selections and alternates before execution.

Use the corrected private-/scratch SweepGA/FastGA contract. A reproducible FastGA-specific failure after one corrected retry must trigger a pinned WFMASH fallback on the exact same staged FASTAs, followed by the same deterministic bidirectional 1:1 contract; it must not become a species exclusion. For graph-ID failures, rebuild alignment/partition inputs from exact staged FASTA dictionaries and resolve only digest-validated aliases; never silently omit regions or treat a tooling mismatch as biological failure.

Mandatory IMPG architecture: IMPG exists to avoid materializing the full graph. Preserve validated H1/H2 alignments and the IMPG partition index, but do not enumerate/query every native partition, materialize an all-genome graph, or perform a global IMPG lace. Cancel any such active workers. Query only bounded, predeclared H1 reference ranges; load only intersecting IMPG partitions; construct the local implicit graph; extract and normalize local variants; audit them; reduce needed statistics; then discard local graph temporaries. Exact GFF intervals should drive bounded annotation queries. Genome-wide pi and PSMC must stream a disjoint contig-aware tiling of bounded reference ranges, with explicit boundary ownership/deduplication and exactly-once callable-base accounting. A whole-genome VCF is optional and, if needed, is assembled by concatenating normalized nonoverlapping range outputs, never by global graph lacing. Historical exhaustive-query/global-lace outputs are diagnostic artifacts only and cannot be promoted.

Before resuming P02/P03 production, run a fresh bounded-range canary against a matching P07 subset and prove identical normalized local variant keys and callable accounting. For all three, produce callable assembly-derived pi, normalized range-local VCF/BCF as needed, consensus blocks, repaired PSMC with 200 centered bootstraps, scenarios, and exact native annotation partitions where cataloged.
